config.title: Frontend Performance & Core Web Vitals

intro.title: Frontend Performance & Core Web Vitals
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple web page that measures and displays key performance metrics known as Core Web Vitals, such as Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) and Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS). You'll learn how to use the PerformanceObserver API in JavaScript to capture these real-time metrics from the browser. The main technologies involved are vanilla JavaScript, HTML for structure, and the browser's built-in performance monitoring tools. By the end, you'll understand how to implement basic performance tracking to improve user experience on your own websites.
intro.usecase: Core Web Vitals directly impact user experience in high-traffic applications like e-commerce product pages, news article feeds, and banking dashboards. Developers optimize Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) to ensure hero images load instantly on retail sites, improve First Input Delay (FID) for responsive search filters on travel booking platforms, and minimize Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) to prevent checkout buttons from moving during payment flows. These metrics are monitored in tools like Google Search Console and directly influence SEO rankings and conversion rates, making performance optimization a critical business requirement rather than just a technical concern.

objectives: Implement performance monitoring by integrating a Core Web Vitals measurement library into a JavaScript application
Configure lazy loading for images and components to reduce initial page load time
Construct a performance budget and apply it to control bundle size and asset optimization
Manipulate the critical rendering path by optimizing CSS delivery and script loading strategies
Initialize and render a virtualized list component to handle large datasets efficiently
Update existing code to implement memoization techniques for expensive function calls
Bind event listeners using debouncing or throttling patterns to improve interaction responsiveness

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from the 'react' package.

// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are available for use in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Create the main PerformanceDashboard component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named PerformanceDashboard that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called PerformanceDashboard that returns null.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the PerformanceDashboard component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A component named PerformanceDashboard is created and returns null.
successCriteria: The PerformanceDashboard component is defined and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the component is named exactly 'PerformanceDashboard' and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you defined a function named PerformanceDashboard that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize performance metrics state
steps.instruction: Inside the PerformanceDashboard component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'metrics' initialized to an object with LCP, FID, and CLS properties all set to 0.
steps.hint: Call useState with the initial object: { LCP: 0, FID: 0, CLS: 0 } and destructure the returned array into a variable and setter.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state object for user data
const [user, setUser] = useState({ name: '', age: 0 });
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a 'metrics' state variable ready to track Core Web Vitals values.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an object containing LCP, FID, and CLS properties initialized to 0, and the returned array is destructured into 'metrics' and 'setMetrics'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're creating a state object with all three properties: LCP, FID, and CLS, each set to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is incorrect. Use useState to create an object with LCP, FID, and CLS properties all initialized to 0.

steps.title: Add the main container structure
steps.instruction: In your PerformanceDashboard component, return a div element with the class name 'performance-dashboard' that contains an h1 heading with the text 'Core Web Vitals Dashboard'.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a JSX structure that includes the div and h1 elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a structured container with a heading that matches the lesson's performance dashboard theme.
successCriteria: The component returns a div with class 'performance-dashboard' containing an h1 with the exact text 'Core Web Vitals Dashboard'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your return statement includes a div with class 'performance-dashboard' and an h1 with the exact title 'Core Web Vitals Dashboard'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The structure doesn't match the requirement. Check that you're returning a div with the correct class and an h1 with the specified text.

steps.title: Display the LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) metric
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your PerformanceDashboard component, add a div element that displays the LCP metric value from your state with a label and unit (ms).
steps.hint: Access the LCP value from your metrics state object and display it inside JSX curly braces.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a value from state
Current score: {score} points
steps.expectedOutcome: The LCP metric value (currently 0) should be displayed in the UI with appropriate labeling.
successCriteria: A div element is added to the return statement that displays the LCP value from state with a label and 'ms' unit.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're displaying the LCP value from your metrics state object with proper labeling and the 'ms' unit.
steps.feedbackWrong: The LCP metric isn't being displayed correctly. Check that you're accessing the lcp property from your metrics state and displaying it with appropriate text.

steps.title: Display the FID (First Input Delay) metric
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add a div element to display the FID metric value from the state. Include a label 'FID:' and show the value with 'ms' unit.
steps.hint: Access the FID value from the metrics state object and display it in JSX.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a state value in JSX
LCP: {metrics.lcp} ms
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now display the FID metric value in the UI.
successCriteria: A div element shows the label 'FID:' followed by the FID value from state and 'ms' unit.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a div, but make sure it displays the FID value from the metrics state with the correct label and unit.
steps.feedbackWrong: The FID metric isn't displayed correctly. Check that you're accessing metrics.fid and including the 'ms' unit.

steps.title: Add the update button and wire it to the handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Simulate New Metrics' inside the main dashboard container, and wire its onClick event to call the updateMetrics function.
steps.hint: Place the button after the metric cards. Use the onClick prop and pass the updateMetrics function reference.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Simulate New Metrics' appears in the dashboard, and clicking it triggers the updateMetrics function to generate new performance metrics.
successCriteria: The button element with text 'Simulate New Metrics' is added to the dashboard container, and its onClick prop is set to call the updateMetrics function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the correct text 'Simulate New Metrics' and the onClick handler is properly wired to the updateMetrics function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly configured. Add a button element with text 'Simulate New Metrics' and wire its onClick to the updateMetrics function.

steps.title: Add performance status indicators
steps.instruction: Inside each metric-card div, add a status indicator that shows 'Good', 'Needs Improvement', or 'Poor' based on Core Web Vitals thresholds. For LCP: Good ≤ 2500ms, Poor > 4000ms. For FID: Good ≤ 100ms, Poor > 300ms. For CLS: Good ≤ 0.1, Poor > 0.25.
steps.hint: You can add a <span> or <div> element with conditional text and styling. Use a ternary operator to check the metric value against thresholds.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each metric card now displays a status indicator (like 'Good', 'Needs Improvement', or 'Poor') based on Core Web Vitals thresholds, providing visual feedback about performance quality.
successCriteria: All three metric cards contain status indicators with correct threshold logic for LCP, FID, and CLS.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some status indicators, but check that all three metrics (LCP, FID, CLS) have indicators with the correct threshold logic.
steps.feedbackWrong: The status indicators are missing or don't use the correct Core Web Vitals thresholds. Review the instruction and try again.
